findings.claim: §12.7.4 describes multi-maintainer Gate 1 as 'machine-enforced' via `required_approving_review_count >= 1` + `require_code_owner_reviews: true` + `require_review_from_non_author: true`, but does NOT require `dismiss_stale_reviews: true`. Without stale-review dismissal, an attacker with PR write access can obtain a CODEOWNER review on an initial commit, then push subsequent commits containing bypass-surface changes (e.g., adding `.scp/rule-config.yaml` with `disable: true`, or adding `scp_bypass: true` to the caller wrapper) after the approval is recorded. GitHub's documented behaviour for `dismiss_stale_reviews: false` + `require_code_owner_reviews: true` when a new commit introduces a CODEOWNERS-protected path is ambiguous: the prior approval from a CODEOWNER for earlier files may satisfy the review count even though the reviewer never saw the malicious new file. The `enable-required-check.sh` helper compounds this: its `build_payload` function splices `$existing_reviews` from the adopter's current state into the PUT body, meaning adopters who have never explicitly configured `dismiss_stale_reviews: true` (the GitHub API default is false) will silently retain a vulnerable review shape after running the helper. The 'machine-enforced' claim in §12.7.4 is therefore conditional on adopters having separately and correctly configured stale-review dismissal — a condition the guidance does not require, check for, or warn about.

findings.impact: An insider or compromised contributor account on a multi-maintainer adopter repo can: (1) open a PR with clean content that passes SCP policy check and gets a CODEOWNER approval; (2) push an additional commit adding `.scp/rule-config.yaml` with `disable: true` for one or more SCP rules after the review; (3) merge without a fresh CODEOWNER review on the new file, depending on GitHub's ambiguous behavior. The SCP-E006 observability annotation emits (non-blocking) but no CODEOWNER approval for the `.scp/rule-config.yaml` change is guaranteed. Gate 1 in multi-maintainer mode is supposed to be the machine-enforcement backstop for the rule-config bypass surface identified in SAFE-009 — if Gate 1 can be circumvented by pushing after review, the SAFE-009 closure (CODEOWNERS-protect rule-config) provides weaker protection than §12.7.4 claims.
findings.mitigation: (1) Add to §12.7.4 multi-maintainer mode description: 'ALSO configure `dismiss_stale_reviews: true` on the adopter branch protection. Without stale review dismissal, an approved PR that receives new commits — including additions of `.scp/rule-config.yaml` or modifications to the caller wrapper — may not require re-review from a CODEOWNER before merge. Stale-review dismissal is the enforcement complement to `require_code_owner_reviews`.' (2) Add to `enable-required-check.sh`: when extracting `$existing_reviews`, check whether `dismiss_stale_reviews` is false (or null) and emit a `WARNING` if so, recommending the adopter set it to true before proceeding. (3) Optionally, when `$existing_reviews` is null (no existing review config), construct a default that includes `dismiss_stale_reviews: true` rather than passing null.

An adopter who reads §11.10 in isolation — which is the natural reading path for adopters configuring the rule-config feature, as §11.10 is the definitional home — would treat CODEOWNERS protection as optional. The §12.7.4 back-reference ('Adopters MUST CODEOWNERS-protect `.scp/rule-config.yaml` (per §11.10)') cites §11.10 as the authority, but §11.10 itself uses weaker normative language, creating a self-referential inconsistency where the MUST points to a section that says 'recommendation'.

findings.mitigation: Upgrade §11.10's CODEOWNERS language from 'CODEOWNERS recommendation' to 'CODEOWNERS requirement (MUST)' and add a rationale sentence: 'CODEOWNERS protection on `.scp/rule-config.yaml` is required (MUST), not optional: `.scp/rule-config.yaml` suppresses rule denies without triggering the three-gate break-glass check (see §12.7.4), making it a bypass-surface equivalent to `scp_bypass: true`. A single developer can silently disable any SCP rule without CODEOWNERS coverage.'

findings.claim: §12.7.13 (supply-chain posture, v1.0.0 disclosure) discloses the Regal SHA256 gap (TF-020H3-001) but receives no forward-reference from §12.7.1 (canonical caller wrapper), §12.7.3 (branch-protection setup), or §12.7.9 (pre-commit hook). An adopter following the natural setup sequence — §12.7.1 → §12.7.2 → §12.7.3, or the pre-commit hook path at §12.7.9 — would complete adoption without encountering the supply-chain risk disclosure at §12.7.13. The gap is that a MAJ-severity known gap (Regal binary executing with GITHUB_TOKEN, no SHA256 verification) is disclosed only in the last substantive sub-section of a 13-sub-section appendix, with no signpost from the earlier setup sections.
findings.evidence: §12.7.1 (canonical wrapper): no mention of §12.7.13; §12.7.3 (branch-protection setup): no mention of §12.7.13; §12.7.9 (pre-commit hook): references SHA-locked OPA and Conftest binaries ('SHA256 verification is performed') but does not note that Regal in the CI workflow is NOT SHA256-verified, nor forward-reference §12.7.13; §12.7.13 text: 'Regal binary downloaded at hardcoded `0.40.0` without SHA256 verification... treat this as a known supply-chain gap until 020H.2 closes it.'
findings.impact: An adopter who reads through §12.7.1 to §12.7.9 to complete setup and does not read §12.7.13 adopts the federation primitive without knowing that: (a) a binary downloading with GITHUB_TOKEN access is unverified; (b) a fork-and-add workaround exists; (c) the gap is tracked as TF-020H3-001 → 020H.2. The §12.7.9 pre-commit hook section specifically mentions SHA-locked binaries in a way that could create a false sense of complete supply-chain coverage, since it does not note that the CI workflow contains an unverified binary. Adopters cannot make an informed risk decision if they don't reach §12.7.13.
findings.mitigation: Add a supply-chain risk forward-reference in §12.7.1 (canonical wrapper), immediately after the YAML snippet: 'Note: before deploying, review §12.7.13 for the v1.0.0 supply-chain posture and the known Regal SHA256 gap (TF-020H3-001).' Similarly, add to §12.7.9 (pre-commit hook), immediately after the SHA-locked binary mention: 'Note: the CI workflow's Regal binary is not yet SHA256-verified (§12.7.13 discloses this gap; tracked as TF-020H3-001 → 020H.2).'

findings.claim: DISPATCH-NOTE TF-020H3-001 records 'closure target = next session' as the deadline for closing the Regal SHA256 supply-chain gap. 'Next session' is not a calendar date, a release milestone, or a dependency condition — it is an open-ended commitment that can drift indefinitely as backlog priorities shift. A MAJ-severity gap (unverified binary executing with GITHUB_TOKEN access on every PR in every adopter repo) should have a concrete closure deadline in both DISPATCH-NOTE and STATUS.md, not a session-relative pointer that loses meaning once the current implementation session ends and the note is read weeks later.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md TF-020H3-001 section: 'closure target = next session'; FIX-ROUND-1.md: 'SAFE-011 (MAJ) — Reviewed mitigation: §12.7.13 added... Tracked as TF-020H3-001 → slice 020H.2'; DISPATCH-NOTE.md post-merge STATUS.md commitment: 'mark 020H part 3 landed with PR # and commit SHA reference' and 'mark TF-D1-001..003 closed' — but TF-020H3-001 is distinct and its STATUS.md entry resolution language is 'next session' not a date.
findings.impact: If 020H.2 is not opened immediately after 020H part 3 merges — due to competing priorities, session boundaries, or backlog pressure — TF-020H3-001 persists in STATUS.md 'Post-Threshold-A backlog' without a forcing function. All adopters who have deployed the v1.0.0 federation primitive continue to run an unverified Regal binary with GITHUB_TOKEN access. The fork-and-add mitigation in §12.7.13 requires per-adopter manual action and breaks Renovate auto-bump, so most adopters will wait for the upstream fix — which has no committed date.
findings.mitigation: Replace 'closure target = next session' in DISPATCH-NOTE TF-020H3-001 with a concrete deadline: 'closure target = before v1.0.1 release OR within 14 calendar days of 020H part 3 merge (whichever comes first); if deferred beyond this window, escalate to user review.' Update STATUS.md 'Post-Threshold-A backlog' entry for TF-020H3-001 to include the same deadline with an absolute date (e.g., 2026-05-14 if 020H part 3 merges 2026-04-30). This gives the next session a forcing function rather than an open-ended backlog item.

findings.claim: D-031 item (c) states `required_approving_review_count = 1` as the anticipated 020D2 configuration for the SCP self-dogfood gate. D-033 corrected D-032's count from 1 to 0 (single-operator self-approval is structurally impossible on GitHub; count=1 locks the sole operator out). D-032's decision text includes a D-033 forward-reference annotation noting this correction. D-031's item (c) lacks a corresponding forward-reference annotation, creating a cross-document state where D-031 and D-033 describe incompatible values (count=1 vs count=0) for the same live configuration parameter without a linking note in D-031.
findings.evidence: D-031 item (c): 'at slice 020D2, branch-protection on `main` is configured with `required_approving_review_count = 1`, `dismiss_stale_reviews: true`, and `require_review_from_non_author = false`'; D-033: 'Updated to count=0 + codeowner_reviews=false in single-operator mode... GitHub forbids PR authors from approving their own PRs'; docs/security/branch-protection.md verify section: `review_count: 0` — the live state confirms count=0; D-032 has an explicit '**Note (D-033 forward-reference, 2026-04-30 evening)**' annotation covering the same correction, absent from D-031.
findings.impact: An operator consulting D-031 (e.g., when preparing to onboard a second maintainer and needing to understand the current baseline before flipping to count=1 + codeowner=true) will read a stale count=1 and potentially misidentify the delta required. Cross-document inconsistency reduces trust in the decision log as a reliable single source of truth for the live branch-protection shape.
findings.mitigation: Add a D-033 forward-reference annotation to D-031 item (c): '**Note (D-033 amendment):** the `required_approving_review_count = 1` anticipated here was corrected to `count = 0` by D-033 (2026-04-30 evening) when the first PR through enforced mode revealed that GitHub forbids PR self-review; count=1 + sole CODEOWNER = operator locks the repo. See D-033 for the live state and the second-maintainer escalation path.'

structured_review.summary: BLOCKED — 1 MAJ finding (SAFE-R2-001) requires resolution before this slice merges. SAFE-R2-001 (MAJ): §12.7.4's 'machine-enforced' Gate 1 claim for multi-maintainer mode is conditional on adopters having configured `dismiss_stale_reviews: true`, which the guidance does not require and the `enable-required-check.sh` helper does not set or warn about. Without stale review dismissal, an attacker with PR write access can obtain a CODEOWNER approval on initial content then push bypass-surface changes (`.scp/rule-config.yaml` disable, caller-wrapper weakening) after the review, exploiting ambiguity in GitHub's CODEOWNERS re-evaluation behavior when `dismiss_stale_reviews: false`. This undermines the SAFE-009 closure's protection guarantee: CODEOWNERS-protecting `.scp/rule-config.yaml` is necessary but not sufficient if the review covering that file can be stale. All R1 SAFE-001..010 and SAFE-012 closures verified genuine at post-fix-round-1 state; SAFE-011 deferral is structurally adequate (§12.7.13 disclosure present) but TF-020H3-001's 'next session' deadline is insufficiently concrete (SAFE-R2-004 MIN). 4 additional MIN/nit findings: §11.10 normative inconsistency (SAFE-R2-002 MIN), §12.7.13 missing forward-reference from §12.7.1 (SAFE-R2-003 MIN), and D-031/D-033 cross-document staleness on count value (SAFE-R2-005 nit). No findings recommend descoping. All mitigations are additive text changes or helper-script warnings.
